title: fix(spec): remove FieldReferenceSchema from the $between endpoints and rule $in/$nin members out (#7596)
body:
Fixes #7596

## The ruling being executed

Maintainer ruling recorded on #7596 (2026-08-11, comment 5250622398), verbatim and untranslated:

> **Ruling: Remove.** Take `FieldReferenceSchema` out of both `$between` endpoint unions, and rule `$in`/`$nin` members out explicitly — declared = enforced via removal (ADR-0049). ⛔ No member-resolution implementation without measured demand (startup-focus): zero consumers today, and two backends already refuse these positions loudly.

## Premise re-verified on `origin/main` @ `6a9dec6` (post-#7672)

| claim | anchor found | note |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `FieldReferenceSchema` in both `$between` endpoints, documentation copy | `packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts:318-321` | as filed |
| ditto, ENFORCED copy | `packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts:822-825` | as the claim comment predicted (`+4` after #7672) |
| `$in` / `$nin` are `z.array(z.any())` | `:222`, `:225` and `:811-812` | a reference was admitted in both copies |
| the evaluator cannot see a list member | `packages/formula/src/matches-filter.ts:382-387` | the issue cited `:342`; the function moved but is byte-identical: `!Array.isArray(raw) && '$field' in raw`, then `return raw` |
| both SQL faces refuse the four list positions | `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/cross-field-conformance-cases.ts:447-468` | the refusal arm, run against both SQL drivers |

Premise holds in full. The `$gt` / `$gte` / `$lt` / `$lte` references (`:197-209`, `:805-808`) are #5222's shipped capability and are untouched.

## What changed

**`packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`** — both copies, from one shared factory each, so the pair cannot drift:

- `$between`: each endpoint is now `rangeEndpointSchema(0 | 1)` — the union `number | Date | string`, no `FieldReferenceSchema`.
- `$in` / `$nin`: `setMembershipSchema('$in' | '$nin')` — still `z.array(z.any())`, with one member shape ruled out by name. The member type is deliberately NOT narrowed: a membership list is heterogeneous and this schema is field-agnostic, so narrowing would refuse working filters (the same finding `RangeOperatorSchema`'s "why a BARE string" section records for the sibling slot).

Both refusals are message-bearing, built by one `listPositionFieldReferenceMessage(position)`:

```
A { "$field": … } reference is not a valid $in member at index 1. No evaluation path
resolves a field reference inside a list: the in-memory evaluator (matchesFilter) leaves
the list unresolved and compares the raw reference OBJECT, so it silently matches nothing,
and both SQL drivers refuse the position with INVALID_FILTER / 400. Write a literal value
here, or move the reference to a scalar comparison operator ($eq/$ne/$gt/$gte/$lt/$lte),
whose WHOLE comparand a { $field } reference may be. Ruled 2026-08-11 on #7596:
declared = enforced (ADR-0049).
```

Consistency with the driver door was measured, not assumed. `crossFieldComparisonError` (`sql-driver.ts:1013`) names the field, the operator and the member index and offers two escapes — "compare against a literal value here, or evaluate the rule in memory (matchesFilter)". The schema-door message keeps the index and the literal escape, and deliberately **drops the in-memory one**: at a list position the memory path is precisely the one that answers with a wrong row set instead of an error, so repeating it would send an author to the only path that fails silently.

### Why the `$between` refusal rides on the union's `error` callback

Measured on zod 4.4.3 in this repo: a `superRefine` attached to the TUPLE does not run once an ELEMENT has failed, so a tuple-level refinement could never see the endpoint it was written to explain. The union's own `error` callback runs exactly when the union rejects, sees the offending input, and returns `undefined` for every other rejection — so endpoint shapes that were already invalid keep zod's wording, `code` and `path` untouched. That is pinned as its own test ("does not repaint the refusals that were already there").

### Docs and comments

`FieldReferenceSchema`'s docblock gains the LIST-positions carve-out; `RangeOperatorSchema` and `SetOperatorSchema` state the ruling; `RANGE_ENDPOINT_DESCRIPTION` no longer advertises the reference. `cross-field-conformance-cases.ts`'s list-position note is updated from "filed as its own finding" to the resolution, with the reason its four refusal cases stay unweakened: the schema door is not on every path to a driver, and a driver that trusted the declaration would answer these shapes with the silent zero-row result #5041 found here in the first place. One comment in `packages/objectql`'s array-lowering test no longer calls a `$field` member "legitimate".

## Sweep for the old position (whole repo, quoted exact names)

`$between` / `$in` / `$nin` carrying `$field`, over `*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `*.md`, `*.mdx`, `*.json`, `*.yml`, `*.yaml`, excluding `node_modules` and `dist`:

| hit | disposition |
| :--- | :--- |
| `packages/spec/src/data/filter.test.ts:244` — `$between: ['2026-01-01', { $field: 'contract.end_date' }]` asserted to PARSE | **flipped** to a refusal pin, in place |
| `packages/spec/src/data/filter.test.ts:254` — `$between: [{ $field: 'a.min' }, { $field: 'a.max' }]` asserted to PARSE | **flipped** to a refusal pin, in place |
| `driver-sql` `cross-field-conformance-cases.ts` (4 cases), `sql-driver-cross-field-reference.test.ts` (4 rows), `sql-driver-silent-empty-predicate.test.ts`, `driver-turso` `remote-transport-comparand-refusal.test.ts` | **kept verbatim** — refusal assertions for shapes that are still, and now doubly, invalid. All typed `unknown`, so no typecheck coupling to the narrowed tuple |
| `packages/objectql/src/engine-filter-array-lowering.test.ts:505` | **kept** — the gate under test judges list-ness, not members; only its comment was corrected |
| `CHANGELOG.md` files, `.changeset/gentle-pumas-repeat.md` | **untouched** — historical records of what #5041 fixed |
| templates / seeds / example apps / stored metadata | **zero hits** |

The positive control for that zero: the same sweep run without the `$field` filter returns the ordinary `$between` usages (temporal conformance corpus, driver tests), so the grep does reach those trees.

## Blast radius

`NormalizedFilterSchema` and `FieldOperatorsSchema` have no runtime `.parse` callers — every reference in the drivers is prose in a docblock quoting the declaration. The typed `Filter[T]` helper already excluded a reference from `$in` / `$nin` / `$between`, so no exported TypeScript type loosens or tightens beyond `FieldOperators['$between']`, whose members go from `number | Date | string | { $field: string }` to `number | Date | string`.

## Tests

New pins in `packages/spec/src/data/filter.test.ts`, in the same describes that carried the acceptance assertions:

- `SetOperatorSchema` → `$field members are refused (#7596)` — `$in` and `$nin`, path and message (index, prescribed alternative, ruling), every offending member reported not just the first, other member shapes still open, enforced copy matches.
- `RangeOperatorSchema` → `$field endpoints are refused (#7596)` — lower bound, upper bound, both bounds, already-invalid shapes not repainted, enforced copy matches, and a positive control that the four ordering slots plus `$eq` still take a reference (#5222) — if that one went red the refusal message would be prescribing something that does not work.

One pin reports an inverted expectation honestly rather than fabricating a red: **`NormalizedFilterSchema` cannot refuse this, and could not refuse anything before this PR either.** A `$and` member is `z.union([z.record(z.string(), FieldOperatorsSchema), NormalizedFilterSchema])`, and the second branch is a non-strict object with every key optional, so it accepts any object at all. Measured control in the same test: `{ $and: [{ close_date: { $null: 'not-a-boolean' } }] }` is equally green and has nothing to do with #7596. Filed separately as #7711.

```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test              377 files / 9892 tests passed
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck         tsc + scripts + test-typecheck OK
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated   13/13 artifacts up to date
pnpm check:driver-conformance                     exit 0
pnpm check:merge-driver / check:adr-anchors / check:spec-parsed-alias   exit 0
driver-sql            86 files / 1399 tests passed (4 files, 50 tests skipped)
driver-sqlite-wasm    24 files / 374 tests passed
objectql             182 files / 3228 tests passed
service-analytics     71 files / 1442 tests passed
typecheck: driver-memory, driver-mongodb, driver-sql, driver-turso, formula, objectql — Done
```

Generated artifacts moved: `content/docs/references/data/filter.mdx` (the two `describe()` strings on `$in` / `$nin`). `check:authorable-surface` is green with no anchor movement — `RangeOperator` and `FieldOperators` are not projected into the tracked authorable surface, so the endpoint-union change moves no baseline.

**Reverse verification, direction predicted before running: RED.** Took the fix out with `git checkout origin/main -- packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts` (no `git stash`), predicting exactly 9 failures — 5 in the `$between` block, 4 in the `$in` / `$nin` block, with `does not repaint`, `leaves every other member shape open` and the `#5222` control staying green. Result: `Tests 9 failed | 119 passed`, the predicted 9 by name. Restored with `git checkout claude/issue-7596-between-list-fieldref-removal -- ...`, back to `128 passed`.

## Changeset

`.changeset/filter-list-field-reference-removed.md`, `@objectstack/spec: major` — this narrows an acceptance surface, and the repo is in changesets pre-mode (`rc`), where the no-major guard stands aside by design and 148 pending changesets already carry `major`.

**ADR-0087 conversion: not-required**, argued in the changeset rather than asserted. No key is retired (`$in`, `$nin`, `$between` all remain with their arity intact), so there is no old shape to convert to a new one; no lossless transform exists, because a `{ $field }` endpoint has no literal equivalent and rewriting it to `{ $gte: ref, $lte: ref }` would not preserve behaviour but invent it — the removed shape evaluated to "matches nothing" in memory and to a 400 on both SQL faces, so any conversion producing rows changes every existing answer; and the blast radius is the measured zero in the sweep table above.
